criteria.text: I can set a prompt-only limit for a named run or a named batch with explicit members, including work that has not started and an existing saved run.
I can inspect the limit and identify the repository, the selected work and the batch members it covers.
The limit remains effective through process, chat, account and PDD restarts or updates. If its applicable state cannot be read or trusted, PDD stops and tells me how to inspect or recover it.
For limited work, PDD can proceed through the prompt PR but stops before allocating a code area, branch or chat, building or publishing code, merging or deploying.
Repeated starts, ticks, opens, approvals and resumes, including reuse of a current saved run, do not bypass the limit or assign the same issue twice.
A routine gate approval, checker pass or release detection does not grant code permission or widen the limit, whether the repository is new or already released.
I can explicitly permit code for selected limited work later, and PDD records the actual permission and its scope. A question, a change request or earlier unrelated approval is not permission.
I can explicitly revoke or extend a limit. Revoking a limit alone does not silently permit code, and an unauthorized request changes neither the limit nor code permission.
Work with no applicable limit retains its existing authorized flow.
